name: Nicodemus
bio: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and ruler of the Jews, came to Jesus by night, acknowledging him as a teacher sent from God because of his miracles. Jesus told him that no one could see the kingdom of God without being born again, of water and the Spirit; when Nicodemus questioned how a grown man could be born again, Jesus explained the Spirit's work as mysterious as the wind, and spoke of the Son of Man being lifted up like Moses's serpent in the wilderness so that whoever believed in him would not perish but have eternal life, declaring that God so loved the world that he gave his only Son for this purpose (John 3:1-21). His further role is told in detail in the chapters ahead. At the Feast of Tabernacles, when the Pharisees scorned the crowd for being deceived by Jesus, Nicodemus, one of their own number, objected that the law required hearing a man out before judging him, and was rebuffed for seemingly defending a Galilean (John 7:45-52). After Jesus's death, Nicodemus joined Joseph of Arimathea in preparing his body, bringing about a hundred pounds of myrrh and aloes to wrap with the linen cloths, according to Jewish burial custom (John 19:39-40).
